clue.text: Friends entertaining obscure fortune tellers

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the friends word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: pals are friends
to mist something is to obscure it, as fog does

explanation.surface: Some friends are playing host to a pair of murky soothsayers.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm readers tell your future from the lines of your hand, so they are a kind of soothsayer.

clue.text: A mate has addiction to drug: time to leave Middle Eastern territory

parts.note: bud is American slang for a mate or friend

indicators.note: the clue tells the letter standing for time to go away from the word for addiction

parts.note: a habit is a drug dependency

explanation.surface: A friend with a drug problem is being kicked out of a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: This emirate is a member state of the UAE on the Persian Gulf, so a Middle Eastern territory.

clue.text: After large amount of whisky, medical officer supplies port

indicators.note: the medical officer's letters are placed after the shortened whisky
a large amount of the word, not all of it, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: malt is a kind of whisky

explanation.surface: After a lot of whisky, the ship's doctor hands out supplies of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts as the drink, after the whisky; it is the Swedish harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city in southern Sweden is a harbour on the Öresund strait, so a port.

clue.text: Many players needed help for broken leg?

explanation.surface: An injured actor needs a crutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors in the secondary roles of a production are many players; a plaster cast holds up a fractured limb.

clue.text: Foreign princess supports concession for singers

indicators.note: in a down clue the princess word sits under, and so holds up, the concession word

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone
a rani is an Indian princess or queen

explanation.surface: A princess from abroad backs a compromise to placate a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural of the highest female voice part names a group of singers.

clue.text: Tribe from exotic land

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A tribe from a faraway country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish family group sharing descent is a kind of tribe.

clue.text: Agreement doctor can set to work

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A treaty that a physician is able to get going on.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal treaty, especially between the Vatican and a state, is a type of agreement.

clue.text: No route specified, nevertheless

explanation.surface: A traveller with no particular road in mind, setting off regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means whichever road you like; as one word it is an adverb meaning regardless.

clue.text: Tower of Pisa, maybe?

parts.note: the famous tower leans, and a leaning structure is one that is tilted, a sense of the adjective for a protected heritage structure

explanation.surface: The famous tilting tower in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective is read as 'leaning', which the Pisa tower is; in Britain the phrase also means a building protected by law for its historic interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure on the official heritage register is protected; the Pisa tower is also a structure that lists, or tilts.

clue.text: Snuggle into bed, perhaps, and feel quite embarrassed

explanation.surface: Someone getting cosy under the duvet while cringing with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie with knees drawn in is to snuggle down; the same phrase also means to cringe with shame.

clue.text: Flexibility of scheme established by Cyprus, involving independence

indicators.note: the scheme word takes in, or involves, the letter for independence

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is a standard abbreviation for independent or independence
CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus

explanation.surface: A flexible plan drawn up by the Cypriot government that includes national independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliancy is the quality of bending easily, which is suppleness or flexibility.

clue.text: Girl's heart breaking, having to conceal love affair

indicators.note: the rearranged heart letters hide the other pieces within them
a breaking heart is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shown as the letter O
a do is a social affair or party

explanation.surface: A woman is heartbroken because she has to keep a romance secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges HEART into THERA, and 'to conceal' puts O and DO inside it, after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, borne by a Byzantine empress, so it names a girl.

clue.text: Tough pair gave orders out loud

indicators.note: the clue says the words for pair and gave orders are spoken, matching another phrase in sound

parts.note: two is a pair; bade is the past tense of bid, to order

explanation.surface: Two hard men shouted their commands.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, TWO BADE matches the phrase entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a dismissive reply, the phrase is like 'Hard luck!', the same sense as the exclamation 'Tough!'.

clue.text: Forgetful best man-one did look silly, having mislaid ring

indicators.note: the words look silly when rearranged, once they have lost one letter

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: The forgetful best man looked a fool when he lost the wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O (ring) from BEST MAN ONE DID and rearrange the twelve letters that remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose mind is elsewhere and who loses track of things is forgetful.

clue.text: I praise team's icon extravagantly

indicators.note: the words are arranged extravagantly, wildly out of order

parts.note: the word team with its s

explanation.surface: A fan gushing over a club's star player.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: one who writes eulogies says 'I praise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who writes or speaks eulogies is a professional praiser, so the clue's 'I praise' is that person speaking.

clue.text: A Greek god with attitude, I assume

parts.note: a pose is a deliberate attitude or stance
to don is to put on, or assume, clothing or a manner

explanation.surface: A Greek deity speaks with a swagger and takes things for granted.
explanation.definitionFit: He ruled the sea in Greek mythology, one of the Olympian deities.

clue.text: A few words from commanding officer, one initially out of order

indicators.note: the letter for one comes out of the front of the order word

parts.note: an instruction is an order
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A commanding officer says a few words to one soldier who is out of line.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a group of words arranged together is a syntactic unit, so a few words.

clue.text: Overturned vat near foreign restaurant

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue, so the vat's letters are read backwards
the letters are made foreign, or strange, by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A vat lies upturned near a restaurant abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' turns VAT into TAV; 'foreign' turns NEAR into ERNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a small Greek eating house, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Kitchen gadget for someone camping?

explanation.surface: A gadget for use on a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camping' is not tents: to camp it up is to behave in a theatrical, effeminate way, and to mince is to walk affectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that chops meat finely is a kitchen gadget; one who walks with dainty affected steps is acting camp.

clue.text: From what we hear, Philip and Michael like the cinema

indicators.note: the clue says the short forms of the names are spoken and match the entry in sound

parts.note: Phil is short for Philip; Mick is short for Michael

explanation.surface: Two friends apparently enjoy going to the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: PHIL and MICK spoken together match the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to film, so cinematic, like the movies.

clue.text: Hamlet character-loathsome king confining prisoner

indicators.note: the words for loathsome and king lock up the prisoner inside them

parts.note: vile means loathsome
a lag is a convict, especially an old lag
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A loathsome king in Shakespeare's play keeps a man locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamlet character' points at Shakespeare's play; a hamlet is a small village, and its character is one of its residents.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small village, so one of its residents is a village dweller.

clue.text: A sum of money levied on island

parts.note: a toll is a charge levied, as for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A charge imposed on an island community.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon is a type of island.

clue.text: Rather vulgar runner can be heard

indicators.note: the clue says the word for runner is spoken and matches the entry in sound

parts.note: a courser is a swift horse, a runner

explanation.surface: A crude athlete makes a lot of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or vulgar, so its comparative form is rather vulgar.

clue.text: Heroine, one without husband, deserted in confinement

annotationWithheld.why: Heroine, one without husband, deserted in confinement: I + SOLE (feme sole, unmarried) fits, but no recognised abbreviation or synonym gives D from 'deserted', and no other parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: Heroine, one without husband, deserted in confinement

clue.text: Dry, yet river goes through it

indicators.note: the river letter passes through the middle of the other word

parts.note: but means yet
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Arid country, though a river runs through it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brut is the label for a very dry champagne or sparkling wine.

clue.text: Californian going round North America on one leg, backwards

indicators.note: the letters for North America turn round, read in reverse
the words one and leg are read backwards

explanation.surface: A Californian hopping round the continent on one leg in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns NA into AN; 'backwards' turns ONE LEG into GELENO.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of Los Angeles, the city in California, is called by this name.
